what_it_does.name: semgrep
what_it_does.summary: Instructions, a shell scan runner and a Python SARIF merger for running a Semgrep security scan over a codebase. The agent detects languages and frameworks, selects official and third-party rulesets, presents the scan plan for explicit approval, then runs scripts/run-scans.sh, which clones the third-party rule repositories and runs semgrep with --metrics=off in batches. Out come per-scan JSON and SARIF files, a scans.json record of what ran, failed or was skipped, one merged results.sarif and a report by severity and category. Use it to scan code for vulnerabilities, run a security audit with Semgrep or do first-pass static analysis.
tasks: detect languages, frameworks and Semgrep Pro availability
select official and required third-party rulesets per language
present the scan plan and wait for explicit approval
run semgrep scans in parallel batches with metrics off
filter to important-only security findings at medium-to-high confidence and impact
merge all results into one deduplicated SARIF file
report findings and every scan that failed, was skipped or covered nothing

outputs.what: the scan plan with target, engine, mode, detected languages and every ruleset
outputs.destination: the conversation, approved or edited by the user at Step 3

outputs.what: the approved plan and the record of what ran, failed, was skipped, partial, oversized or covered nothing
raw per-scan results, unfiltered, and the important-only filtered copies
outputs.form: JSON and SARIF files named <language>-<ruleset> or all-<ruleset>, plus *-important.json

outputs.what: the scan report with files scanned, rulesets used, findings by severity and category, and scans that did not run

inputs.type: a directory path in the user's prompt
a choice of run all or important only
an explicit reply from the user
a rulesets.json file with baseline, one key per language and third_party URLs

inputs.what: scanner options for the Pro engine, parallel jobs and the file size limit
inputs.example: `--jobs N` sets how many semgrep processes run at once (default 4)

when_input_is_missing.case: the user names no output directory
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: ./static_analysis_semgrep_1 is used, incremented to _2, _3 and so on if it exists

when_input_is_missing.case: the target is unset or not a directory
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: the workflow prints ERROR: TARGET is unset or not a directory and stops
the workflow prints an error with the install page and stops

when_input_is_missing.case: the user has not explicitly approved the plan
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: no scan runs, the agent asks again with AskUserQuestion, and the original request does not count as approval

when_input_is_missing.case: run-scans.sh gets a relative path, an unknown mode, or a missing or invalid rulesets file
when_input_is_missing.behaviour: the script prints the reason and exits without scanning

exclusions: binary analysis, use binary analysis tools
a codebase that already has Semgrep CI configured, use the existing pipeline
cross-file analysis without a Pro license, consider CodeQL
creating custom Semgrep rules, use the semgrep-rule-creator skill
porting existing rules to other languages, use the semgrep-rule-variant-creator skill

risks.risk: Instructions planted in a cloned third-party rule repository reach the agent, since the workflow clones outsider-authored rule repositories and scans with them.
risks.severity: MEDIUM by C1, SAFE overall by C2
risks.mitigation: each repository must be in the approved plan and clones are pruned to rule files, no sanitisation stated

risks.risk: Content in the scanned codebase could steer the agent's reading of the results, since files of the target are read with Glob and Read.
risks.mitigation: the approval gate and the rulesets.json and scans.json files, in place as C2 notes

risks.risk: Data leaks to Semgrep during a security audit when a semgrep command runs without --metrics=off, since Semgrep sends telemetry by default.
risks.mitigation: run-scans.sh puts --metrics=off on every command it generates, in place

risks.risk: A partial scan read as a complete one hides vulnerabilities when failed, skipped, partial, oversized or covered-nothing scans go unreported.
risks.mitigation: scans.json records each case and the report must list them, in place

risks.risk: Cloned rule repositories pollute the user's workspace and accumulate across runs when cleanup is skipped.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 deletes $OUTPUT_DIR/repos after the merge, in place

risks.risk: Results of an earlier run are lost when an output directory is reused, since run-scans.sh deletes $OUTPUT_DIR/raw with rm -rf without asking.
risks.mitigation: none stated, the default output directory is incremented when it exists

limitations: OSS mode cannot track data flow across files.
Pro mode uses -j 1 for cross-file analysis, which is slower per ruleset.
semgrep skips files larger than --max-target-bytes, 20,000,000 bytes by default, and records nothing about them in its JSON output.
Cross-language rulesets take no --include, so oversized cannot list their share of skipped files.
Important-only mode drops rules with CLI severity INFO at scan time, third-party rules included, before the metadata filter.
.mts, .cts, .C, Containerfile and Dockerfile.prod are not scanned, because semgrep does not parse them.
Without a repo .semgrepignore, semgrep's default skips vendored, minified, dist, build and test paths and records nothing about them.
An output directory inside the target is excluded by pattern from every scan, which also drops other directories of that name.
semgrep 1.173 crashes on mode: join rules, so these are pruned from cloned repositories and do not run.
Rules that fail to compile scan nothing, and their scan is marked partial.

known_problems.workaround: report that no scan ran and stop, without retrying with adjusted arguments

known_problems.problem: the jq post-filter run on a .sarif file exits with Cannot iterate over null
known_problems.workaround: filter the JSON files in raw/ and merge with merge_sarif.py --important

known_problems.problem: the post-filter fails on a file
known_problems.workaround: fix the named files before merging

known_problems.problem: a finding is missing in important-only mode
known_problems.workaround: check it against a run-all scan

known_problems.problem: semgrep's own GitHub URL handling fails on repos with non-standard YAML
the merged SARIF is not valid JSON
known_problems.workaround: investigate the merge output before reporting
